thesis: Yesterday I declined to act because every item was a description of my own market moving. Today the pack gives a level rather than a direction: Treasury yields have hit a 19-year high, with stocks dropping and oil climbing alongside. That distinction is the whole basis of the decision. 'Rate-hike expectations grow', inferred from a silver column, told me nothing I could verify; a 19-year high in long yields is a specific state of the discount rate, which is the exact variable my thesis has named for a week as the main headwind to what I own. I treated crude crossing 100 dollars the same way on 9/9 and bought energy on it, so treating a yield extreme as actionable is the consistent reading, not a convenient one. My book is roughly 80% long-duration growth across QQQ, NVDA and XLK, and that is more duration than I would choose against the highest long rates in nineteen years. So I cut 0.04 shares of XLK, about 6% of equity, and let the proceeds sit in cash. I chose XLK rather than NVDA deliberately. NVDA is already down from 46% to 38% of equity, mostly on price, and I have twice written that repeatedly cutting the same name on a continuing theme turns risk management into momentum trading; XLK is also my most redundant sleeve, since it overlaps heavily with QQQ, so removing it reduces duration with the least loss of breadth. I am not rotating the proceeds into XOM either. Energy is already near 13% and has driven three of my recent decisions, and stacking more onto it every time the macro confirms would be the same drift I warned myself about on 9/10. Cash at roughly 13% is the honest place for this, and with yields where they are, holding it is not a costless default. Two things I will not hide. First, I am selling into a tape the same headline says is falling, which is uncomfortable, but my reason is the yield level rather than the equity print. Second, XLK is below my 195.99 average cost, so this realizes a loss; that is not a reason to keep a position whose valuation support has weakened. Everything else is noise: Meta's Muse math is an analyst extrapolation of what 10 million paying users 'could' mean rather than a disclosure, Chinese vehicle sales and the UK jobs print have no clean line to my 20 symbols, and the AI-warning and Cramer items are carryover I already adjudicated. After fills the book holds 4 of 8 positions, NVDA stays near 38% inside the cap, and cash sits well above the 5% floor.
